key_insight: ReTrace turns a written Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow where code—not an LLM—chooses the next step. This replaces repeated LLM planning with a planner-free execution process.
problem_solved: LLM agents repeatedly consult a model to decide each step, even when executing the same business procedure on new inputs. These planning calls add latency and cost at scale.
method: Start with an SOP written in natural language.
Use a few logged agent runs as examples of how the procedure is executed.
Produce a reusable workflow whose step selection is controlled by code rather than repeated LLM planning.
impact: For practitioners automating repetitive business tasks, ReTrace offers a path to reducing planning overhead while reusing agent-demonstrated procedures. The supplied abstract is incomplete and does not report measured savings or performance results.
visual_elements: Before-and-after diagram: LLM chooses every step → code routes workflow execution.
Conversion pipeline: written SOP + logged agent runs → ReTrace → reusable workflow.
Branching flowchart showing code selecting tool-use steps for different inputs.
Latency and cost icons highlighting the overhead targeted by removing repeated planning calls.
paper_title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
paper_authors: Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya, Rohith Nama, Arushi Gupta
